text:
Simon Nemec spent 155 games as a Devil, and he walks back into Newark tonight on a five-game point streak (two goals, three assists) in a Calgary sweater. Sportsnet's headline says he returns "with no regrets, improved play." Maxim Tsyplakov, 22 games a Devil, makes the same trip. Neither homecoming is in our numbers, but both give the Flames something to play for beyond a 10% playoff chance in our simulations.

The man in the other net has his own before-and-after. Connor Hellebuyck has been the most written-about Devil for two weeks, between pieces on the Jets since they traded him and CBS Sports saying he is playing his best hockey of the season right now. His season line is ordinary so far (.900 in 11 games, about half a goal saved above expected, which measures goals allowed against the quality of shots faced). New Jersey plays Winnipeg on the back half of a back-to-back, so tomorrow may be the louder night. Tonight the Devils are also without Brenden Dillon, suspended four games, plus Anthony Mantha and Johnathan Kovacevic.

The matchup in net leans hard toward New Jersey. Dustin Wolf has allowed 6.1 more goals than his shots deserved, with an .878 save percentage, and the Devils have taken 56% of the expected goals at five on five, the share of quality chances, against Calgary's 47%. Our numbers give New Jersey 3.90 expected goals to 2.43. Evan Rodrigues is the one to watch: nine points in ten games, and earned, since his own chances are up too. He's our depth sleeper at 20% to score, with Luke Evangelista at 54% for a point. Jack Hughes, white skates and all, is at 42% to score.

Calgary snapped a three-game winless run with a 6-3 win in Pittsburgh, where Jonathan Castagna scored after a staredown with his childhood idol, Sidney Crosby. Martin Pospisil is still out, but Morgan Frost is day-to-day and Connor Zary is off ESPN's injury report, and both returns are in our numbers.
headline: Simon Nemec comes back to Newark on a heater
